title: German Foreign Office to Legation Stockholm, numeric-code telegrams, 2 and 22-27 July 1918 (NARA M367; catalogue 654)

steps.what: Downloaded the telegram frames of M367 rolls 141, 114, 122 and the Christiania cable copies on roll 108; fetched NARA OCR of all four rolls.
Found Mendelsohn, Studies in German Diplomatic Codes (1937) on the Internet Archive after nsa.gov returned 403: 13040, 5950, 26040, the 18470 family, the Dreinummerheft, sliders.
Searched Zeman, Germany and the Revolution in Russia (1958), and the web for these telegrams or a decode: nothing for these days. FRUS not checked page by page.
Transcribed ten telegrams, 938 groups; header counts match on eight and flag truncation on w752 and a shortfall on w643; checked against OCR of frame and cable.
Split into four systems by group range, first-figure index of coincidence and repeats. Found the shared openings 9405 2837 and 23456 21890 in system B.
Plain 13040, 18470-family and Bernstorff 1917 groups against every telegram: exact hits at chance. System D looked close (13049, 13047, 18147 = entziffern) but 3 of 142 hits is chance.
Constant additive -999 to +999 against those sets, the 26040 scheme. Best outliers come from repeated groups and give nonsense.
Slider no. 1 rebuilt from Mendelsohn p. 98, worked example reproduced, all 1000 settings both ways against 13040 and Verkehrsbuch groups. Top settings give nonsense.
18470 groups converted to 12444, 1777, 2310 through the page tables and block shift, with a shuffled-table control: chance. About 125 of 300 pages survive the OCR, so this pass is partial.

Decoded the heads with the Dreinummerheft rule rebuilt from Mendelsohn pp. 5, 21, 29: Nr. 923-925 and Nr. 1010-1015, a consecutive run across three systems; 961 = vom 2 Juli redates despatch 1421 from 22-27 July to about 1-2 July.

outcome.method_basis: No key or skeleton for any of the four systems could be reached, all known German codes printed by Mendelsohn were ruled out, and 938 groups are too few for a ciphertext-only attack.
outcome.notes: Blocked on the code books or the clear drafts. The heads now give the numbers to ask for in the Politisches Archiv.

prior.where: An MI-8 or Room 40 decode may exist (the cables were routed To MID); none located. Mendelsohn 1937 does not mention this traffic.

human: Selected the two catalogue entries and set the goal.
